A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FSPO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite the changed title and added checklist.

before.justification: V1 reports original hallucination evaluations, manual analysis of 200 cases, FSPO benchmark results, and ablation and sensitivity experiments in Sections 2 and 6.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including Table 1 and Figures 1–2 and 4–7.

M1.justification: FSPO retains the same sentence-level factuality rewards, answer reward, token-advantage adjustment, and optimization objective in Equations 8–12. The Reinforce++ adaptation was already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same HotpotQA/2WikiMultiHopQA subset and SimpleRL training data. Evaluation coverage remains GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024/2025, TruthfulQA, HaluEval-QA, and HalluQA, including the same English and Chinese coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the preliminary evaluations and Table 1, including DeepSeek, GPT, QwQ, distilled models, and Qwen/Llama backbones. Figures 4–5 retain the same GRPO, GRPO with factuality, and Reinforce++ comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendices C–F retain the same sample counts, training budget, model configurations, sampling temperatures, metrics, and prompts. No evaluation procedure is added or revised.

E4.justification: Both retain the reward-component ablation, RL-algorithm comparison, 1K–8K training-sample analysis, and response-length/factuality analysis in Figures 4–7. The 200-case error categorization in Figure 2 and Appendix E is also unchanged.

E5.justification: No seed counts, repeated-run details, statistical tests, or uncertainty definitions are added. Figure 7's shading is unchanged. V2's new checklist answers Yes to statistical-significance reporting but supplies only a pointer to the existing experiments.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical entries and the figures' results remain unchanged. For example, FSPO (Qwen-Base) retains 75.5 on MATH-500 and 83.0 on HaluEval-QA. No result entries or qualitative findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Theorems 4.1–4.3 and their proofs, and Equations 1–12 retain the same substance. Differences are limited to mathematical typesetting.

C1.justification: The new title, Reasoning Models Hallucinate More, foregrounds an existing claim. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning RL-associated hallucinations, their theoretical explanation, and FSPO's factuality and reasoning benefits.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and experimental interpretations are retained. Appendices A–B preserve the same binary-reward and model-scale limitations and societal-risk discussion. Replacing factual consistency with factual correctness in Section 6.2 does not substantively change the interpretation.

D1.justification: The implementation framework, HHEM-2.1 verifier, hyperparameters, four H100 80GB GPUs, approximately 24-hour training time, prompt templates, and repository link are unchanged. The checklist points to existing reproducibility information without adding concrete instructions or resources.

R1.justification: The same 46 research references and Section 7 positioning are retained. Bibliographic spacing and page breaks change, but no research work or substantive relationship to prior work is added or removed.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, contact email, and publication notice; makes small wording edits; and adds funding acknowledgments and a standard NeurIPS checklist. The technical exposition and appendix organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: The longer title and added acknowledgments/checklist cause limited reflow and relocate the appendix block. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–4 retain their designs and content, with no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 preserves the same method, proofs, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility details. Its title edits, funding acknowledgment, and checklist mainly update presentation and administrative documentation. The checklist adds no statistical validation, leaving the paper's overall scientific quality effectively unchanged.
